 Charlie Becker secures possessions and avoids disaster as punt returner, but could be gearing up for a greater impact
 Curt Cignetti said this week that he wants more out of the punt return unit
 Andrew Garrison 
 It’s not often that a team’s leading receiver doubles as its punt returner.
 Charlie Becker fills those two roles for No. 9 Indiana, and has for the vast majority of the season.
 “Charlie (Becker), foreign to the position, has done a good job,” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti said on Monday. “I can see the progress every week, and the big thing there is to catch the ball first, because nothing can turn a game around like a punt on the ground.”
 That’s why Becker is back there on punt returns, even now that he’s the team’s top receiver. No matter how far he returns kicks, he catches the ball. Securing possession is what matters most. 
 Charlie Becker receives a punt during Indiana's win over Western Kentucky on Sept. 19, 2026. (HN photo/Lindsey Soet)
 Becker wasn’t always the main man on punt returns. Originally, fellow wide receiver Tyler Morris filled that role. Morris lost the spot when he muffed two punts against Howard in week two, one of which the Bison recovered for fantastic field position.
 Far more often than not, Becker calls a fair catch and safely secures possession. That could partially be because Cignetti doesn’t want Becker, one of the stars of his offense, risking his body more than necessary. Beyond that, in Cignetti's mind, relinquishing the opportunity to rip off a long return in order to avoid risking a turnover is worthwhile trade. 
 No return attempt and no fumble is better than a return attempt and a possible fumble.
 So Becker mostly just calls fair catches. In part because he’s new to the position, and partially in an effort to do his best to avoid disaster. His sole focus is to track the ball, wave his hand in the air, catch the ball and not drop it.
 “Punt returner has been tough,” Becker said on Tuesday. “That’s a hard position. I kind of went in thinking, ‘If I ever got the opportunity, I’m taking one to the crib,’ but getting back there, I’m really just focused on securing the ball and putting our offense in position to be successful.”
 Becker has understandably made some mistakes, as recently as in the game against Minnesota when he called for a fair catch at his own 3-yard line . Still, each week, Becker becomes increasingly more comfortable in the spotlight on special teams. He won’t simply stick to fair catches for long, and Cignetti wants to see increased activity out of Becker on special teams. 
 “Lots of fair catches and possessions of the ball,” Cignetti said about the state of his team’s punt returns. “Would like to get more out of that unit.”
 At first, Becker was just trying to avoid disaster, and he did a good job of that. Even though he’s already the team’s leading receiver and integral to the offense’s success, he seems to be more comfortable with the idea of attempting to return punts for significant gains as the weeks go on.
 “The first thing that comes with anything is securing the ball and making sure our offense has possession,” Becker said, “but watching film and seeing how hard our guys work on holding up, and they do a fantastic job, it’s given me a lot more confidence to return these and put our offense in better field position.”
 Indiana has benefited from lengthy kickoff returns at times this season, in part due to the quality protection in front of the returns. According to Becker, the punt-return unit achieves similar success, which he wants to use to impact games beyond his role as a wide receiver.  
 Muffed punts upend games, but so do punt return touchdowns. It’s clear that Becker can be trusted to not drop the ball, and he’s perhaps poised to prove that he can be a positive force as a punter returner, not just a neutral one.
 “I think I’m starting to build a little bit more confidence,” Becker said, “so when I get my opportunities, I’m going to take them.”
 Becker’s next opportunities as a punt returner arrive this weekend, when he and the Hoosiers host No. 18 USC at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday. Becker’s primary job is to do nothing more than wave his hand in the air and secure possession. He’s not required to do anything more than that. 
 However, against USC, a few lengthy punt returns wouldn’t hurt. Advantageous field position could be especially helpful this Saturday considering Indiana’s uncertain quarterback situation . 
 Maybe Becker sticks to fair catches this Saturday, which wouldn’t be much of an issue. 
 Or maybe Becker tests his luck in open space once or twice, rejoining his teammates after gaining a great amount of yardage before the rest of the offense even stepped on the field.
 If he did, it’d be mighty timely.
